creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares the three big US wireless carriers — T-Mobile (TMUS), Verizon (VZ) and AT&T (T) — as SpaceX and Amazon eye satellite-supported wireless entry. The US wireless market is almost fully saturated, he notes, so the three fight over the same customers, but competition has stayed disciplined, with no race to the bottom on price, keeping the industry lucrative. On expected earnings growth, T-Mobile leads at 18% a year, AT&T is second at 10% and Verizon last at 7%. T-Mobile has focused on its core business and is winning revenue and market share, while Verizon and AT&T spent billions on acquisitions that did not reinvigorate growth. Operating margins are about 24% for the best of the three and around 22% for the other two, all improving since 2017 as prices rose and handset subsidies and support costs fell — though the caption garbles which carrier holds the 24% figure. Debt is heavy across the sector: Verizon over $184bn, AT&T $178bn, T-Mobile $114bn, with a costly 6G build-out ahead. On valuation, T-Mobile trades at 11.9x forward earnings, Verizon at 8.7x, and AT&T's multiple is garbled in the captions. His DCF fair values are $215 for T-Mobile, $57 for Verizon and an unstated figure for AT&T. He calls all three buying opportunities but picks T-Mobile as the best. Calls: TMUS BUY at about $170, VZ BUY at about $44, T BUY at about $22.
